question: Wall outlines can sit several cm inside the real wall (synthetic stain test on c00a170fe1 R2-W6: wall points peak 8 cm behind the outline). A fixed +-5 cm window around the outline then measures the face too far in. Does searching wider for the actual surface help?

baseline.variant: median of points within +-5 cm of the outline (fix loop 1)

variants.variant: nearest histogram peak, 12 cm out / 6 cm in
strongest peak, 12 cm out / 6 cm in
outermost peak, 12 cm out / 6 cm in
most wall-like peak (coverage x height span), 12 / 6 cm
nearest peak, 8 cm out / 4 cm in
measure walls only above furniture height (1.0-2.1 m), outlines from 1.0-2.0 m

decision: Rejected. Every wider search lets the two captures lock onto different surfaces near the wall (curtain, wardrobe face, skirting, the wall itself), so agreement drops from 43% to 12-28%. Kept the +-5 cm window. Its known weakness, inheriting outline error when clutter pulls the outline inwards, is recorded as an open issue: the fix belongs in the outline (wall-line detection), not in the face estimator.
no_signed_scale_bias: Median signed difference per capture pair stays within +-1.1% in every variant, with no consistent sign, so the disagreement is surface selection and local drift, not a scale error between captures.
